problems: The meadow reads predominantly as uniformly maintained lawn.
Vegetation dressing collapses into small coloured discs rather than distinguishable nettles, flowers and rough growth.
Only about 5 tiny clusters on a 12 m tile: one split log, one grey stone with a moss cap, one blue-grey puddle and two specks of flowers. From stream height it reads as empty lawn.

The puddle is the only thing that reads, and its slate colour is close to the grass shadow tone.

elements.fix: Within 30 parts, replace the rails with broad panels carrying chunky interwoven rods between irregular oak posts and occasional stone footings. Keep the boundary 0.7–1.0 m high and the frontage open; hang a small tapered wooden shield with a #d9534f field, one filled household emblem and the exact name 'Ivy' on a pale strip. / Rebuild each run as true wattle. Raise the shield post to 1.6 m and hang a 1.0 × 1.2 m shield at 1.0–1.5 m height, facing +z. Use the owner colour #d9534f for the field and paint a bold cream strip with 4–5 chunky glyph blocks for the name. Pull every part inside |x|,|z| ≤ 6.4. / Pull all parts in to |x|,|z| ≤ 6.3. Move the shield to that front gate post at y 1.5–2.0 and size it 1.4 × 1.2 m: a red field, a pale #e5d8b6 name strip 1.2 × 0.35 m, and one big filled dark emblem (0.4 m) below the strip. No stick-letter glyphs.

problems: The lime's similar-sized foliage balls and evenly fanned shoots create a candelabrum silhouette.
The pear is reduced to a pole and a couple of foliage lobes, with little readable branching.
The 'pollarded lime' is a thick brown stump with thin twigs ending in small green balls; it reads like a cactus or broccoli, not a lime pollard with a dense head of regrowth
The pear is a straight stick with two stacked lime-green spheres: still a lollipop
Neither crown has branches joining it to the trunk; foliage floats as separate balls
The pollarded lime is a thick stump with a fist of thin bare sticks topped by tiny green pom-poms. It reads as a dead hand or broom, not a living tree.
The pear is a sapling with a ~1.5 m blob crown on a thin trunk. Both crowns are smaller than their own shadows.
Together they look sickly next to the cottage in the vignette and give no green mass along the street.
World rule: trees: add an explicit rule that every crown is built from branch boxes carrying several flattened, uneven foliage masses, never a single sphere cluster sitting on a bare trunk.
elements.fix: Redistribute the existing 28 parts into a visibly knuckled pollard with unequal shoot lengths and offset foliage masses. Give the smaller leaning pear one substantial side branch and an asymmetric crown, retaining clearance over the shared frontage. / Lime: keep a 2.8 m knuckled trunk, then build a dense head of 8–10 short, upright, slightly splayed green shoots. Use small flattened cones or boxes in 2 greens (#416c48, #5f8a4a), clustered tightly as a bushy 'broom', with 2 visible cut knuckles. Pear: lean the trunk about 12° toward the road, add 2–3 branch boxes forking from it, and hang 3 overlapping, irregular, flattened foliage masses of different sizes off-centre on the branch ends. Add a few small pale-green pears and white blossom flecks. Make the two trees 4.5 m and 5.5 m tall. / Lime: keep the 2.5 m knuckled trunk (0.6 m thick) and grow a dense, uneven crown from the knuckle. Use 6–8 overlapping low-poly spheres/boxes in two greens (#416c48, #5f8c4a), 1.2–1.8 m each, spreading 4 m wide and 3 m tall, lopsided toward -x. Pear: 4.5 m tall, trunk leaning 12° toward the road, with an asymmetric crown of 4–5 lighter-green (#8eaa62) lumps 3 m wide plus 3–4 tiny pale blossom/fruit dots. Make the two crowns clearly different in height (lime 5.5 m, pear 4.5 m).

problems: The oak has a crooked trunk but a compact crown of similarly sized rounded blobs.
The hawthorn reads as another low shrub, so the group lacks the required tall, broad and low hierarchy.
The 'tall crooked oak' is one straight tilted box with a ball-cluster crown floating on top; there are no limbs, it isn't crooked, and the crown is a symmetric puff
The 'broad hawthorn' is a low clump of light-green balls under 1 m, nowhere near broad
The holly is a small dark ball with red dots; all three read as cartoon blobs, not a woodland margin
The 'crooked oak' is a straight bare plank trunk tilted at about 20°, with a lollipop cluster of 8 spheres balanced on top: exactly the lollipop silhouette to avoid. No branches show.
The 'broad hawthorn' has no trunk and reads as a second ground bush, so the trio is one tree and two blobs.
The holly is a dark sphere cluster with red dots. It's fine, but it sits at the same height as the hawthorn.
World rule: trees: add an explicit rule that every crown is built from branch boxes carrying several flattened, uneven foliage masses, never a single sphere cluster sitting on a bare trunk.
elements.fix: Use the 36 parts for three distinct silhouettes: a crooked oak with exposed lateral limbs and an off-centre broken crown, a medium-height spreading hawthorn with visible branching, and a low dense holly with angular foliage. Avoid repeated spherical clusters. / Oak: build the trunk from 3 boxes that kink (each rotated 10–20° differently), 7–8 m total. Add 3–4 thick limbs spreading sideways, and put 4–5 flattened, uneven foliage masses on the limb ends, offset so the crown is lopsided and wider on one side. Hawthorn: make it 3.5 m wide and 2.5 m tall, with a multi-stem base (3 thin dark trunks) and a flat, wind-swept crown leaning one way, plus white blossom flecks. Holly: make it a 1.6 m dark-green conical, irregular bush built from 3 offset cones with red berries. Vary the greens across the three trees. / Oak: a thick 0.8 m trunk that kinks twice (3 segments), plus 3 heavy branches angled out 35–50° in different directions, each ending in its own foliage mass. That gives a broad, flat-topped crown 7 m wide at 7–8 m height, with gaps between the masses. Hawthorn: a visible short gnarled 2 m trunk splitting into two stems, with a wide, flat, windswept crown 4 m across × 1.6 m tall in a lighter green, plus white blossom dots. Holly/hazel: keep it, but 1.5 m tall and narrower so the three heights differ clearly.

problems: The horse reads as a long plank body on thin sticks, with an underdeveloped neck and chest.
The harness and connection to the passenger cart are not clearly legible.
The hanging wheel emblem becomes an indistinct dark lump in the assembled scene.
The hitching rail with its hanging wheel looks like a small gallows. Its earth pad and bundled luggage are specks, so the 'stop' half does not read as an arrival point.
The cart is shorter than the 5 m brief (about 3.5 m overall). The horse's legs are very thin, and the horse looks pony-sized relative to the cart cover.
2 parts reach outside the 12 m room.
elements.fix: Reallocate the 62 parts to give the horse a substantial chest, wedge-shaped neck, distinct muzzle and thicker planted legs. Add a readable collar, paired shafts and broad harness straps; open up the wheel emblem's centre and spokes, retaining the roughly 5 m overall vehicle length and ground-level hitching area. / Pull the stray parts inside |x|,|z| ≤ 6. Make the stop a 2.2 m hitching frame with two posts and a rail at 1.0 m. Hang the wheel emblem at 2.0 m, enlarged to 0.9 m in a bright painted rim (#d6af55 on dark spokes). Add a bigger worn-earth pad (3 × 1.5 m), a stacked pile of 3 chests/sacks and a mounting block. Lengthen the cart+horse to 5 m. Give the horse 1.6 m withers, 0.18 m legs and a darker mane/tail, with a red-cream cloth on the cart cover's sides so the cart doesn't fade into the grey cobbles.

elements.fix: Within 64 parts, distinguish two fixed planked approaches from a short lowered central leaf with an obvious hinge seam and chains attached to its lifting end. Expose squat stone piers and upstream noses beneath the load path, and add restrained surface bands flowing along x while preserving the specified water extent and bank landings. / Replace the grey box with a timber windlass: a horizontal brown cylinder drum about 0.5 m across, with two dark iron chains (thin #343b40 boxes) running down to the lifting leaf. Make 2 squat stone piers (1.4 m wide, rising 0.6 m above the water, #8a8a7a) with pointed cutwater noses under the joints of the lifting section. Replace the flat oval mats with reed clumps (5–8 thin tall green cones, 0.6–1.0 m tall) and rough grey rocks along the bank edges. Keep all parts within |x|,|z| ≤ 7. / Trim the parts to |x|,|z| ≤ 7. Make the lifting section the same plank colour as the fixed deck (#a87a4c) with a dark seam line only at its two ends. Replace the gantry with one compact A-frame on the near pier (two 3 m posts and a crossbeam) and two visible 0.1 m dark chains running to the lifting leaf's tip. Put the counterweight box on that frame's back end, touching it. Make the stone piers 1.2 × 1.5 m blocks with pointed cutwater noses in pale #c5c0a8. Replace the green water ovals with grey river rocks (#8f948f) and tall reed clumps (dark-green cones 0.8–1.2 m) at the bank edges only.

problems: The large featureless ochre roof reads as a single sheet rather than the specified slate or clay roofing.

elements.fix: Replace the plain roof planes with broad, slightly irregular clay-tile courses and a chunky ridge, using a muted terracotta distinct from the home. Retain the open serving hatch, bread display, masonry cooking feature and sturdy outdoor furniture. / Raise the eaves to 2.6 m so a full storey of half-timbered wall shows under the thatch on all sides. Widen the hatch to 2.4 m with a propped-open shutter board above it and a counter of bread rounds 0.3 m each. problems: Repeated edge patches and hard rectangular ground transitions expose the modular tile construction.

problems: The shaft is a fat round cylinder, 1 m wide and 1 m tall, like a bollard, not a short octagonal market-cross shaft

The thing on the right end (cup/tankard) is a tiny speck.
elements.fix: Make the seat 1.8 × 0.4 × 0.12 m at 0.45 m height. Use two clearly splayed A-trestles, each with 2 legs 0.12 m thick angled 15° outward and protruding 0.15 m past the seat ends, plus one diagonal brace. Darken the legs (#5c4030) against a lighter seat (#a87a4c) so the gap under the seat reads as shadow. Drop the tankard or make it 0.2 m.

problems: The pavilions, awning, brazier and wagon read well, but the knight and minstrel cameos are tiny lumps: the 'knight' is a purple heap with a shield lying flat and the minstrel is a 1 m speck.
The packhorse is small and half hidden behind the right pavilion.
The purple and cream pavilions are the same purple as the awning, with no second heraldic colour, so the court reads as one blob of purple.
elements.fix: Stand the knight upright at full 1.8 m figure scale with a 0.7 m kite shield held at its side in a bright two-colour field (#405e8b / #d6af55), and the minstrel at 1.8 m holding a 0.6 m lute. Move the packhorse 2 m clear of the pavilion to the front-right and make it 1.5 m at the withers. Give the second pavilion a different trim (dark-blue body, gold scalloped valance) so the two shelters are distinct.

problems: The carpenter's mallet reads as a beige lump growing out of his shoulder: the head floats by his ear with no visible handle.
The breadmaker's round loaf floats as a sphere in front of her apron with no hand under it.
The man's green tunic and the woman's red dress read well. The woman's white coif makes her head look too tall and wide.
elements.fix: Put the mallet in his right hand at his side: a 0.5 m handle (#8b6240, 0.06 m) running down from the hand, with a 0.3 × 0.18 × 0.18 m head at the bottom, clearly below the shoulder. Bring the woman's right arm forward (rotate it 40° about x) so her hand sits under the loaf, and flatten the loaf to a 0.3 × 0.16 m disc touching her hand and apron. Trim the coif to 0.38 × 0.22 m so it hugs the head.

problems: The motley is yellow and mid-green. The green half (legs, body, cap) will vanish on the green meadow where the camp sits.
The cap reads as two flaps (red and green) rather than a three-point fool's cap, and the bells are small dots.
The curled shoes are just yellow boxes. The travel patches and court badge are specks.
elements.fix: Recolour the green half of the motley to a strong red (#9e443e) or royal blue (#405e8b) against the yellow. Rebuild the cap as three distinct 0.35 m cones splayed left, right and up, alternating the two motley colours, each tipped with a 0.12 m gold bell. Make the shoes 0.3 m long with a 0.12 m upturned cone toe. Put one 0.18 m bright badge on the chest.

problems: The tail is a straight rigid plank about as long as the body, pointing up and back like a stick stuck into its rump.
The head is good and big. The back has a darker saddle patch that reads as a stray box sitting on top of the back.
elements.fix: Shorten the tail to 0.35 m, set it at 30° above horizontal and taper it (two boxes). Make the darker saddle patch flush with the back (0.02 m proud, not a separate raised block). Keep the mastiff head and dark muzzle.
